THE SPACE CRAFT JOURNAL

Ideas for
better work.

Articles and planning notes on layouts, light, sound, materials and the details that shape a workplace.

Prefer a quick read? ↗
Furniture & workpoints

The workstation is the smallest unit of an office plan.

Desks repeat more than any other element on a floor, so small decisions multiply. Configuration, power, screen height, storage, cables and seating each shape light, sound and comfort across the whole office.

Read the article ↗
Budget & project scope

What really sets the cost of an office interior in Bengaluru.

A per-square-foot figure hides more than it reveals. The cost of a Bengaluru office is set by the building you lease, the services it needs and the ambition of the brief.

Read the article ↗
Meeting & conference spaces

A good meeting room is sized for the meetings that actually happen.

The physical room decides how well people talk. Size, table shape, sightlines, chairs, light, sound and air all matter, and a range of rooms serves most offices better than one large boardroom.

Read the article ↗
Nature & workplace

Office plants survive when they are chosen for the light they will get.

Indian offices are hard on plants: low light, steady air-conditioning, dust and dry weekends. Choose species by light zone, pot them properly and plan their care before they arrive.

Read the article ↗
Planning & layouts

Open or closed is a question about tasks, not about culture.

Companies argue about open and closed offices as if choosing a belief. A clearer approach maps each kind of work by its need for concentration, confidentiality and interaction, then gives it the enclosure it needs.

Read the article ↗
Planning & layouts

From brief to handover: the decisions at each stage of an office project.

An office interior is a sequence of decisions, each made once and built upon. Knowing who decides what, and what should be fixed at each stage, keeps the project moving forward.

Read the article ↗
Nature & workplace

A sustainable fit-out starts with what a tenant can actually change.

Most office tenants cannot alter the building, but the interior is theirs to shape. Knowing where that line falls makes sustainability practical rather than decorative.

Read the article ↗
Planning & layouts

The office design mistakes made early and paid for later.

The costliest errors in an office are rarely visible on opening day. They are decided in the first weeks of planning and felt for the length of the lease.

Read the article ↗
Hybrid & adaptable work

Activity-based working is an operating model before it is a layout.

ABW is often sold as a furniture style. It is better understood as an agreement about how people choose where to work, supported by neighbourhoods, lockers, booking and a clear-desk habit, and tested on one floor first.

Read the article ↗
Planning & layouts

Space planning begins with the floor plate, not the furniture.

An efficient office is decided long before the first desk is drawn. It starts with reading the building you have leased, then fitting the working day to it.

Read the article ↗
Sound & concentration

Living well with the open plan you already have.

Most companies are not about to rebuild their floor. An open office can be made far more workable by moving noisy functions, adding small enclosed rooms, softening surfaces and agreeing how the space is used.

Read the article ↗
Meeting & conference spaces

Meeting rooms changed once half the meeting moved onto a screen.

When some participants join remotely, the room must serve two audiences at once. Cameras, microphones, displays, light and etiquette now shape the meeting space as much as the table does.

Read the article ↗
Arrival & reception

The entrance is a sequence, not a doorway.

First impressions are formed over thirty or forty steps, from the lift lobby to the first view of the office. Each step can be designed, and together they say more than any logo wall.

Read the article ↗
Sound & concentration

Good office acoustics are planned, not bought.

Sound is shaped by where things sit long before any panel goes on a wall. Four simple moves, applied in the right order, decide whether an office can be used for focused work.

Read the article ↗
Ceilings & services

Each room in an office asks something different of its ceiling.

A single ceiling specification across a whole floor is simple to buy and rarely right. Taking the plan room by room reveals what each space needs overhead, and where no ceiling is needed at all.

Read the article ↗
Sound & concentration

The false ceiling is the largest acoustic surface in an office.

A ceiling can absorb noise within a room or stop it passing between rooms, but rarely both by default. Understanding the difference shapes the choice of material, layout and detail.

Read the article ↗
Hybrid & adaptable work

A hybrid office should not have a second class of participant.

When some people join from home and others from the room, the room decides who is heard. Cameras, audio, small call rooms, booking rules and shared tools can make every seat equal.

Read the article ↗
Teams & workplace culture

A breakout space works when it is given a clear purpose.

Breakout areas are often added as a gesture and then left empty. Decide whether the space is for gathering or for recovery, place it accordingly, and furnish it for the settings people actually use.

Read the article ↗
Nature & workplace

The greenest office decisions are often the cheapest ones.

A lower-impact office does not need specialist products. Most of the gains come from keeping what works, buying less, and running the space with care once people move in.

Read the article ↗
Nature & workplace

Biophilic design is about the conditions of a room, not its plants.

Bringing nature into an office means more than adding pots. Views, daylight, natural materials, varied air and the shape of space all connect people to the world outside.

Read the article ↗
Fit-out & renovation

What an office fit-out includes, and how it can be delivered.

A fit-out turns leased floor space into a working office. Knowing what the landlord provides, which trades follow and who carries responsibility makes every later decision clearer.

Read the article ↗
Budget & project scope

Budgeting an office in Gurugram, one phase at a time.

A fit-out budget is not a single number fixed at the start. In Gurugram and the wider NCR, it is a figure set early, tested at each stage and protected by decisions made on time.

Read the article ↗
Arrival & reception

A reception is an operation before it is an image.

The reception desk handles visitors, candidates, couriers, lunch deliveries and staff in a single day. Design it around that traffic, hour by hour, and the appearance will follow.

Read the article ↗
Small spaces

In a small office every square metre has two jobs.

For a team of five to twenty-five, there is no spare room to waste. The best small offices pair functions, build storage into walls, choose one strong material idea and leave space to grow within the lease.

Read the article ↗
Planning & layouts

A layout plan is proven on the floor, not on the screen.

An efficient layout is the one that survives testing. Run competing test fits, draw at true scale, mark a typical cluster in tape on the slab and walk it before anything is ordered.

Read the article ↗
Light & atmosphere

Lighting an office begins at the window and ends at the ceiling.

Good office lighting is a sequence of decisions, starting with daylight and the façade, then layering artificial light, controlling glare and letting the ceiling carry it all.

Read the article ↗
Small spaces

A small office on a modest budget: where to spend and where to hold back.

A limited budget is a question of priorities, not of compromise. Spend where people feel the difference every day, and let the building do the rest.

Read the article ↗
Choosing a design partner

How to choose a workplace design-and-build partner in India.

A ranked list cannot tell you who is right for your office. A clear brief, the right questions and an honest look at who will run your site will.

Read the article ↗
Pantries & shared amenities

An Indian office pantry is designed around tea, tiffins and the lunch hour.

The pantry carries some of the heaviest daily use in the office. Plan it around real habits, from the chai rhythm to the microwave queue, and around the services that keep it clean.

Read the article ↗
Budget & project scope

How to read an office fit-out quotation in Mumbai, line by line.

The total on a quotation is the last thing to look at. In Mumbai, where buildings, permissions and monsoon logistics shape every job, the detail beneath it tells you what you are buying.
